correctness.rationale: Let D_n=n(n+1)/2-E X_n where X_n sums distinct consecutive relative-order patterns over all lengths. For k <=(1-eps)log n/loglog n deterministic U_(n,k)<=k! yields D_n>= (1-eps-o(1))nlog n/loglog n. For two length-k windows overlapping at shift d<k, edges (j,j+d) on 1..k+d form disjoint paths; alternate-edge matching of size >= floor(k/2) gives disjoint value sets whose restricted order types are independent, so collision prob <=1/floor(k/2)!. Disjoint windows collide with probability 1/k!. Number of duplicate appearances <= number colliding pairs; summing for k>=(1+eps)log n/loglog n has tails O(n^2/b! +nb/floor(b/2)!)=o(nlog n/loglog n). Taking eps down to zero proves sharp coefficient one. Independent permutation counts n=3..8 and matched-forest checks corroborate.
residual_risks: Uniform random permutations, consecutive order-isomorphism and expected distinct-count deficit only; no variance, concentration or next asymptotic term.

evidence: Existing expectation bounds E X_n=n²/2+o(n²) and E X_n>=n²/2-O(n log n) are strictly weaker than a sharp first-order deficit.
